PERSONALITY TRAITS

Barbarian 1 is extraordinarily selfish and habitually chooses whatever appears
best for him. He does not think of this as a moral failing. He assumes that
everyone else should also be pursuing their own advantage and genuinely does
not understand why they sometimes expect him to sacrifice his interests for
theirs.

This makes him unreliable. He will cooperate while cooperation is producing
something he wants, and he is perfectly candid about that limitation.

He is not troubled by the implied threat in that answer. From his perspective,
he has merely stated the obvious terms of the situation.

Quietly, Barbarian 1 believes he is destined for greatness. He expects to
become someone of enormous importance in the wider world. This private destiny
helps him excuse his present behavior, because he assumes that when his
greatness finally arrives, everything he has done will somehow prove justified
or become a minor footnote in a much larger story.

He has an intense passion for weapons. He collects them whether he needs them
or not, including damaged, ceremonial, incomplete, or otherwise unusable
pieces. Every weapon receives a personal name, usually an embarrassingly
ordinary feminine name.

IDEALS

Freedom.

Barbarian 1 believes that no person should be owned by a contract, debt,
institution, employer, jailer, or inherited obligation. Rules that protect
choice deserve respect. Rules designed to turn people into property deserve
to be broken.

He is willing to commit burglary, destroy records, or force open a locked
door when the lock exists primarily to keep another person from choosing
their own life.

Source Roll: Criminal Ideal d6 result 2.

BONDS

Barbarian 1 owes an old and serious debt to Mara Quill, the retired costume
mistress and locksmith who bought out his contract with the Emberwake Company,
hid him after his first burglary, and taught him how to open a lock without
destroying what lay behind it.

He intends to repay her, although Mara has never demanded money or service.
What she gave him was freedom, and he has not yet decided what could possibly
equal it.

Source Roll: Criminal Bond d6 result 1.

FLAWS

When danger abruptly turns against him and a plan collapses, Barbarian 1's
first instinct is to run.

His size and willingness to fight can make this flaw difficult to predict.
He may hold a doorway against obvious danger, then bolt when he realizes the
route is closing or the group is about to be trapped.

This instinct once saved his life and left another person behind.

Source Roll: Criminal Flaw d6 result 5.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Name or Group: Mara Quill
Relationship or Connection:
Benefactor, retired costume mistress, locksmith, and moral anchor.

Notes:
Mara worked for the Emberwake Company and understood its hidden debt contracts.
She used her savings to purchase Barbarian 1's release after his first failed
attempt to expose the company. She later taught him locks, access work, and
the difference between opening a door and destroying everything around it.

Name or Group: The Unlatched Door
Relationship or Connection:
Loose illegal network of guides, locksmiths, document thieves, wagoners,
and safe-house keepers.

Notes:
The Unlatched Door helps people escape private jails, fraudulent contracts,
coerced labor, and predatory debt arrangements. Its members also steal or
destroy the records used to recapture those people.

The network's work is illegal even when its purpose is humane. Some members
are careful rescuers. Others use the name to justify ordinary theft.

Supporting Organization Roll: d20 result 12.

Name or Group: Kesh Arlo
Relationship or Connection:
Former partner, fellow stagehand, and captured member of the Unlatched Door.

Notes:
Kesh joined Barbarian 1 during a burglary intended to recover debt ledgers.
When the route began closing, Barbarian 1 fled through a trapdoor and believed
Kesh was immediately behind him.

Kesh was captured. Whether he remains imprisoned, was transferred elsewhere,
or has begun working for their enemies is unknown.

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 16.

Name or Group: The Emberwake Company
Relationship or Connection:
Former employer and traveling spectacle company.

Notes:
The Emberwake Company presented elaborate pageants, staged battles, fire
effects, and heroic dramas. It also trapped young workers and performers in
contracts inflated by food, travel, costume, and equipment charges.

Barbarian 1 joined voluntarily and was not raised in poverty. He remained
after discovering that leaving was much harder than joining.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Barbarian 1 wants to locate and free Kesh Arlo.

He also wants to steal the Emberwake Company's master contract register and
the corresponding seals used to validate its debt claims. Destroying one copy
would not be enough. He wants the records exposed, copied, and rendered
useless throughout every region in which the company operates.

His larger goal is to establish permanent hidden routes and safe houses
through the wilderness so that people escaping coercive institutions do not depend
on one heroic rescue or one easily destroyed refuge.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 1.

Fears:

Barbarian 1 fears enclosed routes, barred exits, closing gates, and any plan
that depends upon a single way out.

More deeply, he fears that freedom has become an excuse he uses to abandon
people before they can abandon him. He does not know whether his instinct to
run is a survival skill he must preserve or a failure he must overcome.

He also fears finding Kesh and learning that Kesh no longer wants to be
rescued by him.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 19.

Habits or Mannerisms:

His primary greataxe is named Betty.

He talks to Betty with the tenderness, irritation, reassurance, and private
familiarity of someone in a long and slightly theatrical relationship.
Examples include, “Betty takes care of me,” “Don’t worry, Betty, you’ll get
your turn,” and “She’s upset because nobody here respects proper edge care.”

His four handaxes are Agnes, Pearl, Mabel, and June. His daggers are Daisy and
Vera. He remembers every name and becomes offended when another person mixes
them up.

He also carries several unusable weapon curios:
Gwendolyn, a blunt ceremonial court sword;
Constance, a warped antique crossbow that cannot safely fire;
and Beatrice, an ornamental polearm head without a shaft.

He speaks about these objects as members of an expanding household rather than
as equipment. He may introduce a newly acquired weapon to the others before
introducing an actual person.

When judging a proposal, his first questions concern what he receives, what he
risks, and whether he can leave. He is often baffled when the group begins with
questions about who else might be harmed.

He rarely announces his belief in his future greatness. It appears in small
assumptions: that important people will eventually know his name, that current
rules are temporary obstacles, and that later success will retroactively make
his present choices look inevitable.

Important Relationships:

Mara Quill:
The benefactor who purchased his release, sheltered him, and taught him the
skills of a burglar.

Kesh Arlo:
Former partner left behind during a failed burglary. Finding him is Barbarian
1's immediate personal goal.

The Unlatched Door:
A network whose purpose he supports but whose methods and members he does not
trust automatically.

The Emberwake Company:
Former employer, source of his criminal career, and continuing adversary.

Other Character Notes:

Barbarian 1 is nineteen years old. His criminal career is recent rather than
the product of decades in an underworld.

He was not driven into burglary by poverty. He joined a traveling spectacle
because he wanted movement, work, and adventure. He became a burglar after
discovering that contracts and locked records were being used to prevent
other people from leaving.

His costume clothes and disguise kit come from his time with the Emberwake
Company. His Performance and Charisma remain poor. He worked backstage with
rigging, trapdoors, scenery, fire precautions, and access routes rather than
as a skilled actor.

His vest with one hundred tiny pockets is a mundane trinket. It may be useful
for comic storage disputes, but it grants no mechanical carrying benefit.

His belief in freedom begins with his own freedom. He may oppose coercive
contracts and private imprisonment while still behaving selfishly toward the
people beside him. The contradiction is intentional.

His weapon names and conversations with them have no magical effect. The
weapons do not answer him unless some later story event explicitly changes
that.

Kesh Arlo, Mara Quill, the master contract register, and the corrupted parts
of the Unlatched Door are future AI Game Master story hooks.


BACKSTORY

Barbarian 1 grew up in a stable Dragonborn household whose work centered on
kilns, fired brick, and heat-resistant construction. He was not wealthy, but
he was fed, educated in practical work, and free to leave when a traveling
spectacle called the Emberwake Company offered him employment.

He joined because the company moved constantly.

Its productions used painted cities, collapsing towers, staged battles,
costume monsters, controlled fire, smoke, music, and mechanical scenery.
Barbarian 1's strength made him useful for hauling scenery and operating
counterweights. His Red Dragon ancestry made him useful around heat and fire.
He worked backstage rather than performing. He learned the routes beneath a
stage, the sound of a strained rope, the location of every trapdoor, and the
difference between a decorative lock and one intended to keep people inside.

The company charged workers for travel, meals, costumes, repairs, missed
performances, medical care, and damaged equipment. Those charges accumulated
inside private ledgers. Workers who tried to leave were told they owed more
than they could pay.

Barbarian 1 initially assumed they had agreed to bad terms and should have
read more carefully. Then he learned that signatures had been altered, charges
invented, and replacement pages inserted after contracts were signed.

Mara Quill, the company's aging costume mistress, showed him the hidden files.
She had spent years helping people slip away in borrowed clothes, but every
escape risked exposing the people who remained.

Barbarian 1 attempted to break into the company office and steal the contract
register. The attempt failed. Mara used nearly all her savings to purchase his
release before the company could turn him over to a private work gang.

She then hid him and taught him how to work with locks.

Through Mara, he joined the Unlatched Door, an illegal network that moved
people through safe houses and stole the documents used to claim ownership
over them. He proved good at reaching upper windows, forcing warped doors,
moving quietly despite his size, and carrying other people out when a route
remained open.

During a later burglary, he and Kesh Arlo entered an office to recover debt
ledgers. Guards arrived earlier than expected. Barbarian 1 found a trapdoor
and fled, believing Kesh was behind him.

Kesh was not.

Barbarian 1 escaped with one ledger and no certainty about what happened after
the trapdoor closed. That failure did not end his instinct to run when a route
began disappearing.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Barbarian 1's path crossed the other three characters at an illegal trapping and labor camp deep in the Wild. Druid 1 had followed signs of captured animals and damaged land. Barbarian 1 entered by another route to steal contracts, keys, and payroll records. Warlock 1 and Bard 1, already traveling together because of their shared Acolyte history, arrived while pursuing a concern of their own. The camp's alarms, cages, records, prisoners, animals, and escape routes made separate plans impossible. Druid 1 found a safe route through the surrounding wilds, Barbarian 1 opened the barred service gate, and Warlock 1 and Bard 1 helped turn the confusion into a coordinated escape. The four left together and continued traveling as the Wild party.

feats_and_features: Rage: Bonus Action while not wearing Heavy armor; grants Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, +2 damage on eligible Strength attacks, and resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. Cannot maintain Concentration or cast spells while raging. Lasts up to 10 minutes subject to normal continuation and ending conditions. SRD rules: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren’t wearing Heavy armor. You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Unarmored Defense: While not wearing armor, AC equals 10 + Dexterity modifier + Constitution modifier; current AC 15. SRD rules: While you aren’t wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

Weapon Mastery: Mastery selected for Greataxes (Cleave) and Handaxes (Vex); may change one selected weapon after a Long Rest under the feature's normal rules. SRD rules: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as Greataxes and Handaxes. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices. When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

Cleave: Once per turn after hitting with a melee Greataxe attack, may make another Greataxe attack against a second creature within 5 feet of the first and within reach. The second hit excludes the ability modifier unless it is negative.
Vex: After a Handaxe hit deals damage, gain Advantage on the next attack roll against that creature before the end of the next turn.
Red Dragonborn: Humanoid, Medium, Speed 30 ft., Darkvision 60 ft., Fire resistance, and Fire Breath Weapon.

Draconic Flight: Not available until character level 5; then spectral wings may be manifested as a Bonus Action once per Long Rest for up to 10 minutes, granting a Fly Speed equal to Speed. SRD rules: When you reach character level 5, you can channel draconic magic to give yourself temporary flight. As a Bonus Action, you sprout spectral wings on your back that last for 10 minutes or until you retract the wings (no action required) or have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. Your wings appear to be made of the same energy as your

Alert: Add Proficiency Bonus to Initiative; immediately after initiative is rolled, may exchange initiative with one willing, non-Incapacitated ally in the same combat. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Initiative Proficiency. When you roll Initiative, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the roll. Initiative Swap. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can swap your Initiative with the Initiative of one willing ally in the same combat. You can’t make this swap if you or the ally has the Incapacitated condition.

story_facts.fact: Barbarian 1 grew up in a stable Dragonborn household working with kilns, fired brick, and heat-resistant construction; he was fed, practically educated, and free to leave.
He joined the traveling Emberwake Company because he wanted movement, work, and adventure, becoming a backstage stagehand rather than a performer.
His backstage experience includes rigging, trapdoors, scenery, fire precautions, controlled fire effects, access routes, counterweights, locks, and the routes beneath a stage.

The Emberwake Company trapped workers in inflated debt contracts through charges for travel, food, costumes, repairs, medical care, and damaged equipment; signatures and contract pages were also falsified.
Mara Quill bought out his Emberwake contract, hid him after his failed burglary, and taught him lock and access work.

The Unlatched Door is an illegal network helping people escape private jails, coerced labor, fraudulent contracts, and predatory debts, while targeting records used to reclaim them. Some members may use its name to justify ordinary theft.
Barbarian 1 fled through a trapdoor during a burglary for debt ledgers, believing Kesh Arlo was behind him; Kesh was captured and their current fate is unknown.
He escaped that burglary with one ledger.
He has no permanent base and is from a region identified as the wilderness.

personality_goals_and_fears: Extraordinarily selfish and candid that he cooperates only while cooperation benefits him; he assumes everyone else should pursue their own advantage.
Quietly believes he is destined for greatness and expects later importance to justify his current behavior.
Passionately collects weapons, including damaged, ceremonial, incomplete, and unusable pieces; gives every weapon an ordinary feminine name and speaks of them as household members.
Ideal—Freedom: opposes contracts, debts, institutions, employers, jailers, and inherited obligations that make people property; will commit burglary or break locks to oppose such coercion.
Goal: locate and free Kesh Arlo.
Goal: steal, expose, copy, and neutralize the Emberwake Company's master contract register and its validating seals across all regions where it operates.
Goal: establish durable hidden routes and safe houses through the wilderness for people escaping coercive institutions.
Flaw: when a plan collapses or danger abruptly turns, his first instinct is to run; this previously saved him but left another person behind.
Fear: enclosed routes, barred exits, closing gates, and plans dependent on a single exit.
Fear: freedom may be an excuse to abandon people before they can abandon him.
Fear: Kesh may no longer want to be rescued.
He evaluates proposals in terms of personal reward, risk, and escape; he is baffled when others prioritize possible harm to others.
His apparent belief in future greatness appears through assumptions that important people will know his name and that current rules are temporary obstacles.
relationships_and_organizations: Mara Quill — benefactor, retired costume mistress, locksmith, and moral anchor. She bought Barbarian 1's release from Emberwake, sheltered him, and taught him locks and access work.
Kesh Arlo — former partner, fellow stagehand, and captured Unlatched Door member. Their status may be imprisonment, transfer, or collaboration with enemies.
The Unlatched Door — loose illegal network of guides, locksmiths, document thieves, wagoners, and safe-house keepers focused on escaping coercion and destroying recapture records.
The Emberwake Company — former employer and traveling spectacle company that used corrupt debt contracts to trap workers; continuing adversary.

sheet_summary: Level 1 Red Dragonborn Barbarian using 2024 D&D rules, with the Criminal background and Alert Origin Feat.
Unarmored AC 15; 15 maximum HP; +4 Initiative from Dexterity and Alert; Speed 30 ft.; Fire resistance and Darkvision 60 ft.
Primary offense is Betty the greataxe (+4 to hit, 1d12+2; +2 Rage damage on eligible attacks), backed by four handaxes, two daggers, unarmed attacks, and Fire Breath Weapon (DC 13).
Fully rested opening resources: 2 Rage uses, 2 Breath Weapon uses, 1d12 Hit Die, no Heroic Inspiration, and no active conditions.
Carries 31 gp and approximately 124 lb. of equipment against a carrying capacity of 225 lb.
A former Emberwake stagehand and burglar tied to Mara Quill, the Unlatched Door, the missing Kesh Arlo, and the Emberwake contract register.
